svg.title: What each rank holds, and the three distributed patterns
svg.desc: A partitioned model part with owned and ghost nodes, and the three things the application does across ranks: gather to rank 0 for export, halo-partitioned subgraphs for data-parallel graph training, and one ShardTensor for domain parallelism.

g.text: a partitioned ModelPart
rank 0 owns
rank 1 owns
interface nodes: owned by one rank, a ghost on the other;
elements are owned, never ghosted
1. Gather to rank 0 - the exporters
GatherFieldToRank0: owned rows only (ghost-free), concatenated and re-sorted by id on rank 0 =
the serial layout, so a distributed run writes byte-identical samples.
GatherModelPartToRank0: a shadow model part rebuilt on rank 0 with the full topology, for the
mesh, CAE and USD exporters; re-gathered every step deliberately, so moving meshes stay correct.
GlobalNumberOfNodes() and every gather are collectives: call them on all ranks, never inside a rank-0 guard.
Metis is not needed by the test suite: a per-rank-slab fixture plus ParallelFillCommunicator builds the partition.
2. Halo-partitioned graphs - data-parallel training
BuildGraph on a distributed part is quietly wrong: rank subgraphs overlap
(local + ghost nodes) and neighbourhoods are truncated at the interface.
BuildHaloSubgraph: owned nodes plus the halo of elements touching them,
exchanging connectivity and coordinates across ranks. Owned sets partition
the nodes exactly; one-hop aggregation matches the serial run everywhere.
Edge ownership follows ELEMENT ownership - a min-rule on node ranks drops edges.
DDP over gloo coexists with a live Kratos MPI run; gradients bit-identical across ranks.
3. One ShardTensor - domain parallelism
ShardKratosField: each rank's owned rows become one uneven shard of a
single tensor over a 1-D DeviceMesh built explicitly on CPU (or CUDA).
ShardGridAlongAxis: a replicated grid split into halo-exchanging slabs,
so a 3x3 convolution equals the serial one. WriteShardedField: owners
first, then the ghost refresh.
The backward of a mean already leaves the serial gradient on every rank.
Verified at np = 2 and 3 over gloo; NCCL needs two GPUs and is untested here.
